subject: Day 1: In the beginning, and the oldest book
body:
Good morning.

Today is the day, and this plan starts differently. You will read creation through Babel, and then jump straight into Job, because Job likely lived in the age of the patriarchs. The oldest questions in the world show up on day one: who is God, and can I trust Him when everything falls apart?

Do not try to solve Job today. Just listen to him.

Heather

subject: Day 2: God answers, and Abraham is called
body:
Good morning.

God finally speaks to Job today, and He does not explain Himself. He just shows Himself. Somehow that is enough.

Then the story narrows to one man. God calls Abraham with a promise that will carry the whole rest of the Bible.

Heather

subject: Day 3: Joseph, and out of Egypt
body:
Good morning.

Watch what God does with a broken family today. Jacob's sons sell their brother, and God uses it to save them all. What people mean for evil, God means for good.

Then four hundred years pass in a page, and God hears His people crying in Egypt. The Red Sea parts today.

Heather

subject: Day 4: Sinai
body:
Good morning.

Today God comes down on a mountain and a nation of freed slaves learns who He is. The Ten Commandments, the golden calf, and a tabernacle so God can live among His people.

Every detail of that tent is God saying the same thing: I want to be near you.

Heather

subject: Day 5: Holy, and into the wilderness
body:
Good morning.

Push through Leviticus today. It reads like a manual, but underneath every rule is a holy God teaching people how to live close to Him.

Then the wilderness begins, and so does the grumbling. Watch how patient God is with people who keep forgetting what He just did.

Heather

subject: Day 6: A donkey, a prophet, and a retold story
body:
Good morning.

Balaam gets rebuked by his own donkey today, which is worth the price of admission.

Then Deuteronomy begins: Moses, at the end of his life, retelling the whole story to a new generation. Remember, he says, over and over. Do not forget.

Heather

subject: Day 7: Goodbye Moses. Hello Promised Land.
body:
Good morning.

One week in. Today Moses blesses the people, climbs a mountain, sees the land he will never enter, and dies. It is one of the most moving pages in the Bible.

And then, after forty years, they cross the Jordan. Be strong and courageous. God keeps His promises.

Heather

subject: Day 8: The spiral, and a faithful few
body:
Good morning.

Judges is dark. Everyone does what is right in their own eyes, and it goes exactly how you would expect.

But right in the middle of that mess, Ruth stays. Hannah prays. A boy named Samuel hears God's voice in the night. God always keeps a light on.

Heather

subject: Day 9: David, and songs from the caves
body:
Good morning.

Today a shepherd boy is anointed king, drops a giant, and then spends years running for his life.

Here is what makes this plan special: you will read the psalms David wrote while it was happening. The caves produced the songs. Hard seasons still do.

Heather

subject: Day 10: The songbook, part one
body:
Good morning.

A lighter day. Just psalms, and most of them David's. Fear, praise, anger, trust, sometimes all four in one song.

Read a few of them out loud. They were written to be prayed, not studied.

Heather

subject: Day 11: The king at his best and worst
body:
Good morning.

David becomes king today, and the Bible does not clean him up for us. Bathsheba. Absalom. All of it.

What sets David apart is not that he never fell. It is that he always came back. Psalm 51 was written out of the worst of it, and you will feel that today.

Heather

subject: Day 12: The record
body:
Good morning.

Chronicles retells David's story from after the exile, when the people needed to remember who they were. Read the genealogies fast. They are there to say one thing: God kept the line going.

Asaph's psalms today ask the honest question: why do the wicked prosper? Sit with his answer in Psalm 73.

Heather

subject: Day 13: Songs across generations
body:
Good morning.

Fifty psalms today, but they move fast. Watch for Psalm 90, the oldest one, written by Moses himself. And Psalm 119, a love letter to God's Word from someone who needed it to survive.

You are almost halfway. Keep showing up.

Heather

subject: Day 14: Praise, then Proverbs
body:
Good morning.

The psalter ends the only way it could: let everything that has breath praise the Lord.

Then Solomon starts talking, and it is intensely practical. Money, words, anger, friendship, work. Wisdom is just holiness with its sleeves rolled up.

Heather

subject: Day 15: Wisdom, honesty, and love
reading: Proverbs 23–31, Ecclesiastes 1–12, Song of Solomon 1–8, 1 Kings 1–4
body:
Good morning.

Three books from one family today. Proverbs finishes with wisdom, Ecclesiastes is the most brutally honest book in the Bible, and Song of Solomon is a love song God was not embarrassed to include.

Then Solomon takes the throne, and asks God for the one thing that matters.

Heather
chapters: Proverbs 23–31, Ecclesiastes 1–12, Song of Solomon 1–8, 1 Kings 1–4

subject: Day 16: The temple, then the tear
body:
Good morning.

Solomon builds the most magnificent temple the world had seen, and the glory of God fills it. And then, a few chapters later, his heart drifts and the kingdom tears in two.

It is a warning worth hearing: nobody drifts toward God. Drift always goes the other way.

Heather

subject: Day 17: Elijah, Elisha, and the runaway prophet
body:
Good morning.

Jonah runs from God today and gets carried back. Amos thunders about justice. And Elijah hands his mantle to Elisha as the kings keep spiraling.

You will also read Chronicles' record of Judah's kings from the same years. Two tellings of one era: Kings shows what happened, Chronicles shows what God was watching for.

Heather

subject: Day 18: Isaiah sees the Holy One
body:
Good morning.

Isaiah sees the Lord high and lifted up, and it undoes him. Today you also read about the very kings he preached under: Uzziah, Jotham, and Ahaz, side by side with his words to them.

Watch for chapter 9. Seven hundred years early: for unto us a child is born.

Heather

subject: Day 19: Comfort, and a love that will not quit
body:
Good morning.

Isaiah 53 is today. Read it slowly. He was pierced for our transgressions, written centuries before the cross.

Then Hosea, the prophet who married a woman who kept leaving him, because God wanted His people to feel what their unfaithfulness felt like, and how relentless His love is anyway.

Heather

subject: Day 20: The fall, and one last good king
body:
Good morning.

Heavy reading today. The northern kingdom falls. Hezekiah prays and God moves. Young Josiah finds the lost Book of the Law and tears his robes when he hears it read. One more revival, and then Jerusalem burns.

Micah tells you what God actually requires: do justice, love mercy, walk humbly. Do not rush past the grief today. The exile is where some of the Bible's deepest hope gets forged.

Heather

subject: Day 21: The warnings before the end
body:
Good morning.

Habakkuk asks God the question we all ask: how long? And he ends up singing anyway. Though the fig tree does not bud, yet I will rejoice.

Then Jeremiah, the prophet who preached his whole life to people who would not listen, and kept going. Faithfulness is not the same as success.

Heather

subject: Day 22: Weeping, and a new covenant
body:
Good morning.

Hidden inside the saddest stretch of the Old Testament is Jeremiah 31: I will make a new covenant. I will write my law on their hearts. That promise is why you are holding a Bible today.

And Lamentations, written in the rubble: great is His faithfulness. His mercies are new every morning. That verse was not written on a good day.

Heather

subject: Day 23: Visions by the river
body:
Good morning.

Ezekiel is exile literature. Wheels within wheels, a scroll he has to eat, the glory of God leaving the temple. Strange and stunning.

Watch for chapter 36: I will give you a new heart, and put a new spirit in you. God is not done.

Heather

subject: Day 24: Dry bones, lions, and a queen
body:
Good morning.

Can these bones live? God says watch me.

Daniel keeps his window open toward Jerusalem no matter what it costs, and Esther risks everything for such a time as this. God's name never appears in her book. His fingerprints are on every page.

Heather

subject: Day 25: Home, and then silence
body:
Good morning.

The exiles come home today and rebuild from rubble, with Haggai and Zechariah preaching at their backs.

Malachi gets the last word of the Old Testament. And then four hundred years of silence. You just read the entire Old Testament, in the order it happened. Tomorrow, He arrives.

Heather

subject: Day 26: He arrives
body:
Good morning.

After everything you have read, all the promises, all the waiting, today He comes. Born in Bethlehem like Micah said, out of Egypt like Hosea said, the child Isaiah promised.

You will feel the difference reading it this way. The whole story has been leaning toward this.

Heather

subject: Day 27: The story, told deeper
body:
Good morning.

Luke notices the people nobody else sees. John pulls the camera all the way back: in the beginning was the Word.

You will read the cross and the empty tomb more than once in these days. It hits different every time.

Heather

subject: Day 28: The upper room, and the explosion
body:
Good morning.

Jesus washes feet, prays for you by name in John 17, dies, and rises. Then the Spirit falls and the church explodes across the map.

Acts ends mid-stride on purpose. The story keeps going. You are in it.

Heather

subject: Day 29: The earliest letters
reading: James 1–5, Galatians 1–6, 1 Thessalonians 1–5, 2 Thessalonians 1–3, 1 Corinthians 1–16, 2 Corinthians 1–13
body:
Good morning.

Now you read the letters in roughly the order they were written, starting with James, likely the first. Faith with hands and feet.

Love is patient, love is kind. Paul wrote that to a church that was tearing itself apart. These letters were written to real messes, which is why they still fit ours.

Heather
chapters: James 1–5, Galatians 1–6, 1 Thessalonians 1–5, 2 Thessalonians 1–3, 1 Corinthians 1–16, 2 Corinthians 1–13

subject: Day 30: To the churches, and to his sons
reading: Romans 1–16, Ephesians 1–6, Philippians 1–4, Colossians 1–4, Philemon 1, 1 Timothy 1–6, Titus 1–3, 2 Timothy 1–4
body:
Good morning.

Romans today: nothing can separate us from the love of God. Philippians, the most joyful book in the Bible, written from a prison cell.

And Paul's last letter, to Timothy: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race. Tomorrow, you finish yours.

Heather
chapters: Romans 1–16, Ephesians 1–6, Philippians 1–4, Colossians 1–4, Philemon 1, 1 Timothy 1–6, Titus 1–3, 2 Timothy 1–4

subject: Day 31: You did it.
reading: Hebrews 1–13, 1 Peter 1–5, 2 Peter 1–3, Jude 1, 1 John 1–5, 2 John 1, 3 John 1, Revelation 1–22
body:
Good morning.

Hebrews 11 is the faith hall of fame, and you have now read every one of their stories in order. You are surrounded by that great cloud of witnesses today.

And then the end that is really a beginning: no more tears, no more death, He makes all things new. The story that started in a garden ends in a city, with God dwelling among His people.

You just read the entire Bible in 31 days, in the order it happened. I am so proud of you. Thank you for reading alongside me.

With love,
Heather
chapters: Hebrews 1–13, 1 Peter 1–5, 2 Peter 1–3, Jude 1, 1 John 1–5, 2 John 1, 3 John 1, Revelation 1–22
